doc.title: Håkan Rydin interviewed by Monk Rowe, Glasgow, Scotland, July 27, 2016

title: Teaching approach and the skills students need today
summary: He teaches by ear and plays together on two Steinways; students also need business and online skills.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Well let’s suppose I had a grandson who was 15.
And really wanted to be a jazz musician, and I sent him to you for some advice.

It wouldn’t be so much work. What I do, I do a lot of playing together. In my room at the school I have two good Steinway grand pianos. So we play a lot together. I teach a lot by ear. I teach songs by ear. It takes a little longer time but I reach some other things that you don’t when you only go by the paper. So that’s what I do a lot.
Do you think students today need to have other skills than the jazz musician of the 1950s?

They have to have knowledge about society. Maybe you needed it at that time, but I mean how to get a gig, how to write a contract, and things like that. How to manage your home page and YouTube and all that kind of stuff maybe. I think that’s needed today. Most of us don’t have someone to do it.
